Crypto doesn't require trust or even knowledge of who the the people are in a financial transaction so there is no corrupt middle man like a bank.

Problem with crypto is that a government could declare it illegal for many reasons including competing currency laws; making for a very risky investment.  There are also other factors like price manipulation through pump and dump events and corrupt brokers who sell the crypto.

First and foremost though, while there are plenty of similar scams that can be this easy, what he described here is called “card present” fraud and is NOT something banks just wave away and take your word for. Especially not for 10k. There is no law that says banks have to cover any and all fraud losses for you. Most practically follow a zero dollar liability policy, but not for 10k events. 

Today we file a dispute on such things and an investigation is launched and we’ll have video of that post office transaction in days. Plus, the account owner would need to fill out an affidavit at the very least, if not also a police report. Yeah, the account opener used a fake ID to open an account with no problem, but while that’s low stakes fraud, lying to the police steps it up to criminal and the second person makes it also a conspiracy. 

One MIGHT be able to pull this off today, but boy you’d be playing with fire and it would take weeks to get money back if it happened at all. Also, you’d burn that fake ID name, and the one used at the post office, as bot would end up on a federal suspicious activity report. So you better be on the run and have a healthy supply of new names and IDs.

comment_text: @johndor7793 It all started In the Summer of 2022 when I received a message from who I thought was this one woman I was looking at (I won't say who, because I'm still not positive it was actually her).  We started chatting on a regular basis and everything seemed to be going well. We hit it off great and there were no money requests ... yet.  Around the Fall of 2022 is when the money requests started.  I protested as best I could, but they knew the right buttons to push and eventually, I always caved.  I found myself trapped in this highly toxic dynamic due to being convinced of what was supposedly the light at the end of the tunnel; but over time, the money piled up on their end, and I went completely broke.  But that didn't stop them.  They kept pressing me for money to contribute to their music videos (which they showed me after the fact).  Whoever this was also had a few people call me with regards to a Miami property they claimed they were getting ready for us.  But that's where I knew not to cross the line and I never signed anything (the only good decision I made during this whole escapade).  As time went on, their money requests kept coming and my protesting, and therefore our arguments, got more and more intense.  But they always found a way to convince me of their legitimacy and I stayed broke, and kept falling behind on my bills.  It ruined my credit and there was one instance where they led me on a money errand that involved a $13,000 deposit into my account, and an immediate withdrawal request of $12,500.  This was the big con!  After I carried out the request and deposited the cash into their BTC account, the bank rejected the deposit and my checking account ended up at around -$11,000.  I presented the texts to the bank and filed a police report; but I kept in contact with this person, still holding out hope that they were real.  Finally, after nearly a year of being used and exploited, I finally put an end to our communication; and I've been working on rebuilding myself, ever since.  They always said that they would pay me back with interest; but of course, as I discovered, that was all a lie to keep me involved in their scam.  In short, this literally ruined my entire life.
